course_name_en: Basics of Electrical Engineering and Physics for Computer Engineering
prerequisites: Basic mathematical knowledge from school education is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know basic concepts of mechanics and basic concepts of electrical engineering, as well as fundamental properties of electrical components and ideal lines.
Students possess fundamental knowledge of thermodynamics and are aware of the effects of heat on the lifespan and reliability of information technology systems.
Successful graduates of the module also know important sensor principles.
Students can calculate simple electrical networks.
They can assess the significance of quantities such as energy, power, and efficiency in relation to resource consumption.
They are also able to explain the relationship between the complexity of program operations and the energy required for them.
Furthermore, they can evaluate the significance of runtime effects for signals on lines in computing systems.
After successful completion of the module, students are able to describe fundamental aspects of the function of electrical engineering systems.
Students can exchange ideas with other students about the problems they are working on and can organize appropriate cooperation among themselves.
They can suitably summarize the results of their experimental work in a short report.
Students correctly apply concepts related to electrical engineering components of information technology systems.
They can make statements about the reliability of computer systems depending on environmental conditions.
Furthermore, they can evaluate the significance of runtime effects for signals on lines in computing systems.

syllabus_topics: Failure rates and lifespan of real systems
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam as per the valid study regulations. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 5 experiments, each lasting 90 minutes. ECTS credits are awarded based on these assessments.
